area: FIT WITH THE SITE: how a "Related projects and alternative approaches" section fits the LabConstrictor-Site code, data files, DESIGN.md rules, checks and the planned citation work

facts.statement: Plain, compact entries linking straight to the GitHub repositories of DL4MicEverywhere, JupyterLab Desktop, ZeroCostDL4Mic and BiaPy would break the site's rules.
facts.evidence: DESIGN.md 'Links': the GitHub pill is the only way to link to a repository. check_design.link_problems fails any <main> link whose href matches REPO_ROOT (https://github.com/owner/repo) unless it has class lc-gh or lc-card__main. AGENTS.md says the same (cards.github_badge). Four of the proposal's seven URLs are GitHub repository roots, so they must be pills. The other three (repo2docker docs, mybinder.org, Voila docs) are not repository roots.

facts.statement: The Ecosystem page is built by pages_site.page_ecosystem from projects.resolve(ecosystem) and has no hook for a second data file.
facts.evidence: pages_site.py lines 84-94 and build_site.py line 85: pages_site.page_ecosystem(projects.resolve(ecosystem)). Headings are h1, then one h2.lc-tier with id=<tier key> per tier (site/ecosystem/index.html has ids 'hosts' and 'dev'). A logos footnote closes the page. edit_url is data/ecosystem.yaml only.

facts.statement: Line budgets: pages_site.py and projects.py are far from the 300-line limit, but tests/test_site.py is not.
facts.evidence: wc -l: pages_site.py 101, projects.py 68, build_site.py 95 (main() is about 26 of 30 allowed lines), cards.py 135, text.py 74, llms.py 27, check_design.py 201, check_site.py 187, pages_apps.py 208, tests/test_site.py 271 (limit 300 applies to tests too, per tests/test_code_rules.py SOURCES), tests/test_design.py 76. The citation plan will add about 30 lines to pages_site.py for the home page cite band.

facts.statement: Hand-written data/*.yaml files here are validated in Python with fail(), not with JSON schemas. schema/ holds only contracts for outside authors, and the whole folder is published at /schema/.
facts.evidence: projects.inline_card checks an exact key set and calls fail(); redirects.check does the same. schema/ has labconstrictor-app, labconstrictor-project and registry-entry schemas. write_sitemap.py line 55 does shutil.copytree(SCHEMA, SITE/'schema'), so a new schema file would be published publicly. config.load_yaml already fails on a missing, unparsable or empty file.

facts.statement: The proposal's 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor et al. (2024) ... Nature Methods 21, 925-927, DOI 10.1038/s41592-024-02295-6' is correct.
facts.evidence: Crossref API for 10.1038/s41592-024-02295-6: title 'DL4MicEverywhere: deep learning for microscopy made flexible, shareable and reproducible', container Nature Methods, volume 21, issue 6, pages 925-927, issued 2024-05-17, first author given 'Iván', family 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor'. Caveat: Crossref's 24-author list contains one empty author entry and 'Mariana G. Ferreira' twice, so a reference must never be generated from Crossref; hand-copy only the first author as 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor et al.'.

facts.statement: The LabConstrictor preprint title and DOI are correct (arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704).
facts.evidence: The arXiv API returns the same title, v1 published 2026-03-11, categories cs.SE and q-bio.QM, and the five authors Iván Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Marcela Xiomara Rivera Pineda, Bruno M. Saraiva, Ricardo Henriques, Guillaume Jacquemet. DataCite (api.datacite.org) confirms DOI, title, publisher arXiv, resourceTypeGeneral Preprint, year 2026. Crossref cannot verify this DOI because arXiv DOIs are registered at DataCite (Crossref returned a non-JSON error). It is a preprint, so the site must not call it a journal article.

facts.statement: The DL4MicEverywhere description (Docker containers, a graphical launcher, local and remote computing incl. HPC) matches its README.
facts.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com HenriquesLab/DL4MicEverywhere README: 'utilizes Docker containers to ensure portability and reproducibility', run locally 'or remotely on ... workstations, high-performance computing (HPC), and cloud-based systems', and 'Double-click the launcher ... A GUI will automatically pop up'. github.com and api.github.com returned 403 through the proxy; raw README fetches worked.

facts.statement: The JupyterLab Desktop, ZeroCostDL4Mic and BiaPy descriptions are accurate.
facts.evidence: JupyterLab Desktop README: 'cross-platform desktop application for JupyterLab' and each launch can use its own Python environment (--python-path). ZeroCostDL4Mic README: Colab notebooks with a graphical interface, computing at no cost. BiaPy README: 'open source library and application' for deep-learning bioimage workflows, with a Docker image workflow badge. The proposal's 'GUIs and containers' for BiaPy was not confirmed in the text I fetched (only the first 40 lines were read). Not checked here: Voila's 'hiding code and exposing widgets' and repo2docker/Binder wording beyond the home pages.

facts.statement: The proposal spells the project 'Voila'. The project's own name has a diacritic.
facts.evidence: voila.readthedocs.io (v0.5.8) writes 'Voilà' throughout ('Installing Voilà', 'convert a Jupyter Notebook into an interactive dashboard'). The YAML must be UTF-8 with 'Voilà'. config.load_yaml and the stylesheet font handle it, and there is a test to add.

curl -L: repo2docker.readthedocs.io, mybinder.org and voila.readthedocs.io return 200 (redirecting to /en/latest/ and /en/stable/). The four GitHub repositories could not be fetched via github.com (403 from the proxy) but their raw README files returned 200 for DL4MicEverywhere, jupyterlab-desktop, ZeroCostDL4Mic and BiaPy, so the owner/name pairs exist.

facts.statement: The proposal's 'repo2docker and Binder' table row is one project.
facts.evidence: They are two projects with two different links (repo2docker docs and mybinder.org). One row would force one link kind, or two ambiguous pills. It is better as two entries.

facts.statement: The citation plan (planning/results/3-citation/PLAN.json) puts the LabConstrictor preprint DOI in one place: site.yaml 'citation.doi', shown on the home page as h2#cite 'Cite LabConstrictor' with the action link 'Read the preprint' and a 'doi:' line. App pages get h2#cite 'How to cite' with link text 'doi:{doi}' and the action link 'Read the paper'.
facts.evidence: PLAN.json implement_now items 1 and 2. Current state: data/site.yaml has links.citation_doi = https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20758747 (a dead key with no reader), and overrides/main.html line 100 hard-codes the same stale 0.0.2 version DOI. A Zenodo record must not be reused as the preprint DOI.

facts.statement: The Ecosystem page's logos note and DESIGN.md's logo rule need no change if the related section shows no logos.
facts.evidence: pages_site.page_ecosystem builds the note from hosts.load() plus hosts.load_services(). hosts.yaml entries require a 'plugin' repository (host_of_plugin, HOST_GUIDES), so related projects must not be added there. The proposal itself says 'no logos'. The GitHub mark in pills is already used on the page.

facts.statement: No other check beyond the existing ones is needed for a new section on the existing page: check_site, menu, reach, description rules.
facts.evidence: The page /ecosystem/ already has one active menu entry and is 1 click from home (home links 'Explore the ecosystem'). check_design.duplicate_descriptions covers description uniqueness (current description 'Hosts, tools and templates around LabConstrictor.' is 49 chars, allowed 20-200). check_design heading_problems requires only no skipped level (h2 then h3 is fine). Outside links get target=_blank rel=noopener from Page.fix_links and finish_site.py, so none is hand-written.

findings:
DECISIONS

1. Where. Add a section at the bottom of the existing Ecosystem page (above the logos footnote), not a new page. Reasons: no new top-menu entry or reach path is needed. It is already 1 click from home. Public addresses are untouched. check_site and check_design already cover the page. The anchor is h2 id="related", so /ecosystem/#related becomes a stable address (note it in DESIGN.md). Group sub-sections are h3 with id="related-<key>". Heading order is h1, h2.lc-tier (tiers), h2 (related), h3 (groups). A new test asserts all ids on the page are unique, so a tier key can never collide with 'related' or 'related-*'.

2. Data source of truth. New hand-written file data/related-projects.yaml. This is our wording about other people's projects, so AGENTS.md 'Sources of truth' gets a bullet saying it is written only here and links to each project's own repository, docs or paper. Do not put these in data/ecosystem.yaml, whose job is 'which of our repositories to list', or in data/hosts.yaml, whose entries require a 'plugin' repository and drive logos and host pills.

3. Validation: Python, no JSON schema. Precedent: every hand-written data/*.yaml (ecosystem inline cards, redirects, hubs) is checked in Python with fail() naming the file. schema/ is for outside authors' contracts and write_sitemap.py publishes the whole folder at /schema/, so a new schema would publish a public contract nobody consumes. Load with config.load_yaml, which already fails on a missing, unparsable or empty file. Exception to revisit: if the maintainers want one error listing every problem, use validate.check with a schema in schema/ and accept the public file.

4. Proposed schema (checked in related.py, exact key sets, no defaults, no .get(key, default)):
   top level: title, intro, groups, closing (all required, no others).
   group: key (slug, unique), title, items (non-empty list); optional text.
   entry required: name (2-40 chars), approach (20-200), use (20-200).
   entry optional: repo ('owner/name'), docs (https URL), site (https URL), doi ('10.NNNN/...'), reference (30-300 chars).
   Rules: at least one of repo/docs/site; docs/site may not be a GitHub repository root (use repo, so the pill rule cannot be bypassed in data); doi and reference come together; no 'http(s)://', '[', ']', '<' or '>' in any prose field (prose is escaped, never linked, and page.decorate_links would turn a '[x](https://github.com/o/r)' pattern into a pill); names unique across the file; optional ban-list for volatile claims (stars, downloads, fastest, best, most popular, faster, superior) to encode 'avoid volatile claims'. This replaces the proposal's single 'url' field, which cannot express GitHub-pill versus text-link rendering.

5. Rendering vs 'plain compact entries'. Decision: keep the proposal's compact, logo-free list but make the links pills. Each entry is an li in a ul.lc-related with: bold name (not a link), approach sentence, 'Useful when: ...' sentence, optional 'Paper: <reference> doi:...' line, then the pills. GitHub repo link: cards.github_badge(repo). docs: cards.link_pill(url, f'{name} documentation', 'docs') (book mark). site: cards.link_pill(url, hostname, 'web'). Pill labels name the project so they are not ambiguous out of context (several pills would otherwise all read 'Documentation'). Do not use ecosystem cards (lc-card): too heavy and the whole-card link would need a second link for the repo. Card/pill rules are all met and check_design needs no change. Intro, group titles and closing text come from the data file via text.esc. Secondary examples (ZeroCostDL4Mic, BiaPy) are a second group 'Other microscopy projects' (h3) so they are not read as notebook-packaging alternatives; the four main comparisons are the first group.

6. 'Choosing an approach' list: do not add a second list. It restates the proposal's 'When it may be useful' column in different words, which breaks single source of truth. The 'use' field is the choosing aid (written as a need). The 'not mutually exclusive' sentence becomes the `closing` paragraph. If a visible list is demanded later, generate it from the same 'use' fields (no extra data).

7. Further reading and the two DOIs. The DL4MicEverywhere paper is shown inside its entry (reference + doi). The LabConstrictor preprint DOI must not be written in related-projects.yaml. Per the citation plan it lives once in data/site.yaml 'citation.doi' and is shown on the home page #cite block. The closing paragraph links to it with an internal text link 'Cite LabConstrictor' to home #cite (write target as 'index.md#cite' so zensical rewrites it; 'zensical build --strict' and check_site's anchor check will catch a wrong form; do not use 'index.html#cite' or '#cite'). Add one shared pure helper `doi_url(doi)` in text.py (validates '10.' pattern, percent-quotes) and `doi_link(doi)` in cards.py: a text link whose text is 'doi:<doi>' and href https://doi.org/<doi>. The home cite band, the app 'How to cite' section and the related entries all use it, so every DOI is displayed identically; whichever change lands first adds it. Sequence: do the related section after citation item 1, or ship it without any LabConstrictor DOI. Do not reuse links.citation_doi (a stale Zenodo 0.0.2 version DOI). Call the preprint 'arXiv preprint', not a journal paper. Never generate references from Crossref or DataCite; hand-copy from the primary record, as the citation plan requires.

8. Page description and lead. The current description 'Hosts, tools and templates around LabConstrictor.' is still unique but now incomplete. Suggest 'Hosts, tools and templates around LabConstrictor, plus other open-source ways to share and reproduce scientific software.' (about 120 chars, unique, within 20-200). It is hard-coded in pages_site.page_ecosystem (DESIGN.md says other pages keep it in a data file; pre-existing deviation, optional cleanup: move it to ecosystem.yaml). Keep the lead 'Everything around the apps...'; the new section carries its own intro saying it is about other people's projects.

9. Edit link. The page footer 'Edit this page on GitHub' stays on data/ecosystem.yaml (precedent: cards' text already lives in other repositories). Add in the section's closing helper line (lc-small) a text link 'Edit this list on GitHub' to {REPO}/edit/main/data/related-projects.yaml so the 'points to where the text is written' rule stays honest. Document this in DESIGN.md. check_site's edit-link rule only flags links into docs/.

10. Logos. No logos for related projects (matches the proposal); the Ecosystem logos note stays as is because nothing new is shown. Add a DESIGN.md sentence under Images: related projects are shown without logos; if one is ever added it needs its own entry type, never hosts.yaml. A test asserts the rendered section contains no <img.

11. Home page / Docs link. Not warranted now. Home already links 'Explore the ecosystem'; the comparison is secondary to the two paths (find an app / make an app), and the planned Cite band shares the home page. Do not add Docs/Use/Build cards. Only update the llms.py Ecosystem line to mention 'and related projects'. Revisit a text link in the Build hub intro after launch if visitors ask 'why not Binder?'.

12. External link rot. check_site skips external links and the build is offline by design (AGENTS 'Two stages'). Do not add a network link check to the daily build (a third-party outage must not stop publishing). Mitigate with the data file header comment (date each URL and the DOI were last checked against its primary record) and, optionally later, a separate non-blocking scheduled link check.

Tests: (a) the real data file passes related.check and contains 'Voilà' and 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor' with diacritics intact; (b) failure cases, each asserting SystemExit text names data/related-projects.yaml and the entry: missing file, unknown or missing top-level key, entry missing name/approach/use, extra key, too-short/too-long text, no link at all, repo not 'owner/name', docs or site not https, docs or site that is a GitHub repo root, duplicate names, duplicate group keys, empty items, malformed doi, doi without reference and reference without doi, URL or '[' ']' or '<' in prose, banned volatile words; (c) rendering: repo gives class lc-gh with href https://github.com/..., docs pill has book mark, site pill label is the hostname, doi link href is https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02295-6, a name or approach containing <script> and quotes is escaped, no '<img' in the section, one h2 and one h3 per group; (d) integration: put the rendered HTML through Page.fix_links and check_design.Facts, then check_design.link_problems and heading_problems return nothing (outside links open in a new tab, no unpilled repo link, no skipped heading), and the page's ids are unique; (e) text.doi_url accepts '10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704' and '10.1038/s41592-024-02295-6' and rejects 'https://doi.org/x', '' and 'doi:10.1/x'.

ORDER OF WORK: DESIGN.md pattern first (AGENTS.md rule), then data file and related.py with tests (failure cases first), then rendering and CSS, then docs files; run the full 'Before you push' sequence.
recommendations: Add the section at the bottom of /ecosystem/ (h2 id=related, h3 per group), above the logos footnote; no new page, menu entry or home/Docs link; update the llms.txt Ecosystem line only.

Create data/related-projects.yaml (title, intro, groups[key,title,text?,items], closing). Entry keys: name, approach, use required; repo, docs, site, doi, reference optional; at least one link; docs/site may not be a GitHub repo root.

Validate in a new scripts/lcsite/related.py with Python fail() messages, not a JSON schema (precedent: ecosystem/redirects/hubs; schema/ is published at /schema/ for outside authors only). Reject URLs and [ ] < > in prose and duplicate names/keys.

Render entries as a compact logo-free list: bold non-link name, approach, 'Useful when', optional paper line, then pills: cards.github_badge for repos, cards.link_pill (docs book, or hostname) for other links; do not use ecosystem cards. This resolves the pill-versus-plain conflict and passes check_design unchanged.
Split 'repo2docker and Binder' into two entries; spell 'Voilà' with the grave accent; keep ZeroCostDL4Mic and BiaPy in a separate secondary group.
Drop the separate 'Choosing an approach' list (it duplicates the 'use' field); keep the 'not mutually exclusive' sentence as the closing paragraph.

Show DOIs through one shared helper (text.doi_url + cards.doi_link, text 'doi:<doi>' linking https://doi.org/<doi>) used by the home cite band, app How-to-cite and the related entries. Keep the LabConstrictor preprint DOI only in site.yaml citation.doi and link to home #cite from the closing line (as 'index.md#cite'); never reuse links.citation_doi (stale Zenodo version DOI). Implement after citation item 1.
Put the tests in a new tests/test_related.py (test_site.py is at 271 lines); include every validation failure, escaping, no-, doi link, and a check_design link/heading integration test.
Update DESIGN.md (pattern, Images sentence, enforcement row) before code, plus AGENTS.md (page table, Sources of truth) and README.md (what it does, edit table).

Extend the Ecosystem page description (unique, 20-200 chars) and add a text link 'Edit this list on GitHub' to data/related-projects.yaml in the section's helper line; keep the footer Edit link on ecosystem.yaml.

Hand-copy bibliographic data from Crossref/DataCite records (Iván Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Nature Methods 21, 925-927 for DL4MicEverywhere); record last-checked dates in the data file header; no network link check in the build.
risks: Conflict of interest and neutrality: several preprint authors (Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Henriques, Jacquemet) are also authors of the DL4MicEverywhere paper (Crossref author list), so the section is about a closely related group's tool. The proposal's key message ('overlapping problems, different technologies, neither better') is safe, but readers may assume independence; maintainers should decide whether to state the relationship in one neutral sentence.

Link rot and drift: seven external URLs and one paper reference live only in our data file and nothing in the offline build checks them; descriptions of other projects can go stale when they change (e.g. Binder service terms, JupyterLab Desktop features). Mitigated by neutral, non-volatile wording, last-checked dates and no popularity/performance claims; not eliminated.

Citation duplication: if related-projects.yaml also carries the LabConstrictor preprint DOI it becomes a third copy next to site.yaml and the template README, and the existing links.citation_doi/footer DOI already point to a stale Zenodo 0.0.2 record. Sequence after citation item 1 and keep one source.

The internal link to home #cite from a generated depth-0 page is untested: Page.u does not rewrite '#cite' or 'index.html#cite' correctly (it would resolve to the Ecosystem page or /ecosystem/index.html). 'index.md#cite' is the expected zensical form; zensical --strict and check_site's anchor check will fail the build if wrong, so the risk is rework, not a silent break.
A page written from two data files makes 'Edit this page' ambiguous; the helper-line edit link is a small new convention that DESIGN.md must record or reviewers will flag it.

Unverified description details: Voilà 'hides code and exposes widgets', repo2docker/Binder wording beyond the home pages, and BiaPy 'GUIs and containers' were not confirmed in this fit review (GitHub web/API blocked by the proxy; only raw README heads read). Do not copy the proposal's wording into YAML until the fact-check areas confirm it.

Crossref author data for the DL4MicEverywhere paper has an empty author and a duplicated name, and arXiv DOIs are not in Crossref (DataCite): any automated reference generation would publish wrong data, so none is proposed.
The site is currently noindex; at launch (extra.listed true) the comparison page becomes public text naming other projects, so the neutral-wording rule matters more then.
open_questions: Should the preprint DOI appear in the related section at all, or only via the home #cite link? (Recommended: only via the link, to keep one source.)
Does the team want a neutral sentence disclosing that DL4MicEverywhere and LabConstrictor share authors, or leave it out?
Are the maintainers content with the extra edit link in the section helper line, or should the footer Edit link be the only one?

Should repo2docker and Binder also get GitHub pills (jupyterhub/repo2docker, jupyterhub/binderhub) and Voilà (voila-dashboards/voila)? These repositories could not be verified through the GitHub API here, so none was proposed beyond the proposal's URLs.
Do the maintainers prefer a JSON schema in schema/ (one error listing everything, but published at /schema/) over the Python checks recommended here?
Exact English wording of each 'approach' and 'use' sentence, and the intro and closing text, awaits the fact-check areas; this review fixes only the structure and rules.
Whether to move the Ecosystem description and lead into data/ecosystem.yaml now (DESIGN.md says pages keep them in a data file) or leave that deviation out of scope.
